title: What If You Met the Person You Could Have Been?

meta.topic: the person you could have been

scenes.narration: What if you met the person you could have been?
Not a stranger. You. Same face, same start, but every chance you talked yourself out of, taken.
You would know him in an instant.
And honestly, it would break your heart a little.
So picture this. One completely ordinary night, there is a knock at your door.
You open it. And you are standing face to face with yourself.
But he looks lighter. Like he sleeps well. Like he isn't carrying the weight you carry.
Hey, he says, in your own voice. I'm the version that didn't wait.
He doesn't gloat. He just steps inside, like he has been here before.
And he offers to show you the life you almost lived.
So you follow yourself, down a long hallway of every choice you ever postponed.
He sent the message you left sitting in your drafts for three whole years.
He started the thing before he felt ready. You are still waiting to feel ready.
He let people watch him be a beginner. So he actually got to become something.
On the hard mornings, he kept the promise to himself. That was the entire secret.
Not talent. Not luck. Just a refusal to quietly break his own word.
And those tiny kept promises stacked up into a life that actually feels like his.
You walk through his days. It isn't glamorous. It's just, lived. On purpose.
His body is strong, because he moved on the days he most wanted to quit.
His work is good, because he was willing to be bad at it first, in public.
His friendships run deep, because he said the honest, terrifying thing out loud.
He isn't richer in money. He's richer in time he simply refused to waste.
And everything he has, you can see the exact door he walked through to get it.
Because you stood in front of those same doors. You remember every single one.
You just told yourself, not yet. Maybe tomorrow. Maybe once it feels safe.
You wait for him to look down on you. He never does.
He is not smarter than you. Not braver. Not born any luckier.
He just flinched a little less, a thousand quiet times, at a thousand small forks.
That is the whole distance between you and him. A pile of tiny moments.
Each one so small it felt like it couldn't matter. Together, they built a different person.
Then he tells you the thing you weren't ready to hear.
I'm not actually real yet, he says.
I am just the sum of the choices you haven't made.
Every day you wait, I drift a little further out of reach.
But every time you choose forward, even badly, I take one step closer to you.
He isn't a ghost haunting your past. He is a direction, waiting in your future.
And then he says, quietly, there's a third one of us, you know.
The version who stopped completely. Who stayed exactly here, and called it being safe.
He isn't lazy. He's just frightened, and he's gotten very good at hiding it.
Every single morning, you wake up standing between the two of them.
And you decide, with one small choice, which one you take a step toward.
So how do you actually close the gap? Not in one heroic leap.
You don't become him in a day. You become him in a single decision.
Pick the one thing he would do today. Only one.
Do it badly. Do it scared. Do it anyway.
Not the whole staircase. You only ever have to see the very next step.
And stop waiting for motivation. It never leads. It follows you, after you begin.
Do the brave small thing first, and the feeling you wanted shows up right behind it.
You will never meet the person you could have been in a doorway.
You meet him in your calendar. In the boring Tuesday. In the choice nobody claps for.
He is always standing exactly one brave decision away from where you are now.
And the beautiful part? You still have time to become him.
Not someday. Not once it's perfect. With the very next thing you choose to do.
So tell me below. What is the one choice the other you would make today? Then go make it.
